title: Formula Book
oneLiner: Phone notebook for hair colourists to save each client's colour formula and history, offline, with a file export

evidence.claim: Gloss, an app that only saves client colour formulas, charges $3.99 a month or $35.99 a year and has 622 ratings averaging 4.6 on the US App Store.
Charm, another formula keeping app, sells premium at $3.99 to $5.99 a month or $34.99 to $45.99 a year, and a reviewer says it refused to save client notes.
Gap: Gloss reviewers in Jan to Mar 2025 report formulas hidden after an update, lost edit and delete, and wrong sums in formulas, so stylists fear losing records held only inside a paid app.
Goldie offers a free hair colour mixing calculator but saving a mix to a client profile needs its paid salon app, so the free tool does not keep history.

nextAction: Research. Target searches: hair color formula tracker, client color formula card, hair color formula log template; the first page for these was app store listings and small salon supply blogs, no big free web tool, but no volume source yet. Against: app stores own the intent and several free tiers exist (Charm, Gloss free month, FyleStyle), salon booking suites already store formulas, and paper client cards sell cheaply at SalonCentric (https://www.saloncentric.com/fromm-stylist-client-profile-cards.html). Distribution through our own pages is the weak part.
